name: Bazedoxifene
lead: Bazedoxifene is a third-generation selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) of the 2-phenylindole class, taken by mouth. It is used for the prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis and, combined with conjugated estrogens as Duavee or Duavive, for menopausal vasomotor symptoms.[1][2] Its appearance connection runs through bone and body composition: by acting like estrogen in bone while blocking it in other tissues, it is a hormone-pathway drug of the type that hormone and physique communities discuss when they talk about SERMs.

A 3-year randomized trial in 6,847 women with osteoporosis found fewer new vertebral fractures than placebo.[3] The combination product Duavee carries a boxed warning about endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia.[2] Published trials concern menopause, bone and, more recently, brain and cancer research; studies in people using it for physique or looks have not been published.
On T Nation, bazedoxifene was raised in 2013 as a new SERM from Pfizer under FDA review, and an earlier thread on Clomid and Nolvadex mentioned it among newer SERMs being evaluated.[12][13]
infobox: Conbriza, Viviant; with conjugated estrogens: Duavee, Duavive

paras: Bazedoxifene alone is used in some countries to prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis, offered as an alternative for women who cannot or prefer not to use bisphosphonates [1]. In the US it is available only in combination with conjugated estrogens, for moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis in women with a uterus [2].

In four placebo-controlled trials of the combination product, adverse reactions at 5% or more included muscle spasms, nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, upper abdominal pain, throat pain, dizziness and neck pain [2]. The label boxed warning covers endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia, and the product is contraindicated in pregnancy [2].

Bazedoxifene binds estrogen receptors and acts as an agonist or antagonist depending on the tissue [1]. Preclinical work reported that it bound estrogen receptor alpha, increased bone density and strength in rats and had limited effects on the uterus and breast cancer cell proliferation [5].

A 3-year randomized, placebo- and raloxifene-controlled trial in 6,847 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis found a significantly lower incidence of new vertebral fractures with bazedoxifene 20 or 40 mg than placebo, with secondary endpoints including nonvertebral fractures, bone mineral density and bone turnover markers.[3] A 2-year report from the same programme described effects on bone density and turnover compared with placebo and raloxifene.[14] The two large phase 3 registrations enrolled about 7,600 and 1,700 women.[11][15]

Network meta-analyses of fracture-prevention drugs include bazedoxifene among SERMs.[6] Trials of bazedoxifene combined with conjugated estrogens examined menopausal symptoms, metabolic parameters and bone-loss prevention in at-risk postmenopausal women.[7][8][16] A randomized trial in postmenopausal women with rheumatoid arthritis on low-dose glucocorticoids examined bone loss with bazedoxifene plus calcium and vitamin D.[17][10]

Other registered or published work includes remyelination in multiple sclerosis (the Re-WRAP trial design and a 63-participant phase 2 study), a phase 4 study in women with schizophrenia, a breast cancer study combining it with palbociclib, and pilot studies of estrogen plus bazedoxifene on depressive symptoms in perimenopause.[9][18][19][20][21][22] Large post-marketing surveillance studies of Viviant in Japan enrolled over 3,000 patients each.[23][24] No study of bazedoxifene for appearance purposes was found.

The European Medicines Agency approved bazedoxifene on 27 April 2009, and the US FDA approved it in 2013 as part of Duavee; Pfizer is listed as developer [1]. Phase 3 osteoporosis trials began around 2001 [11].

An Endocrinology review published in 2005 described it as a SERM with improved selectivity, and a 2013 pharmacology review places it within the lineage of SERMs from tamoxifen onward.[5][25] Bazedoxifene is known by the development codes TSE-424 and WAY-140424, and its name was first paired with conjugated estrogens in the 'tissue-selective estrogen complex' concept used in Duavee.[1][8]
Bazedoxifene is being studied for breast and pancreatic cancer, with a 2013 report describing growth inhibition of breast cancer cells including resistant tumors [1].

Brand names are Conbriza and Viviant for bazedoxifene alone and Duavee or Duavive for the combination; it is prescription-only.[1] In the US, Duavee is labelled for women with a uterus and is contraindicated in pregnancy.[2] The Australian Prescriber review of conjugated oestrogens/bazedoxifene is one clinician-facing summary of the combination.[26]

In forum culture, bazedoxifene appears mainly as a name in discussion of newer SERMs. A 2013 T Nation poster described it as a third-generation SERM under FDA review and said it was thought able to 'destroy estrogen receptor sites', asking whether anyone had experience with it.[12]

timeline.event: FDA approves Duavee (bazedoxifene with conjugated estrogens) [1].

lore.intro: Bazedoxifene is mentioned occasionally in T Nation threads about SERMs such as Clomid and Nolvadex.[13][12]

claims.claim: Bazedoxifene is a newer SERM that could reduce estrogen receptor activity with fewer side effects than older SERMs
claims.believers: A 2013 T Nation poster described it as a third-generation SERM from Pfizer under FDA review and asked whether it could block estrogen receptors; an earlier thread listed it among newer SERMs being evaluated with the hope of reducing risk.[12][13]
claims.experts: Bazedoxifene binds estrogen receptors and acts as an agonist or antagonist depending on tissue; in trials it lowered vertebral fracture incidence in postmenopausal women, and the combination product carries a boxed warning.[1][3][2]

card.summary: A menopause and osteoporosis SERM; nothing in the literature ties it to looks.
card.note: US product is a combination with conjugated estrogens and has a boxed warning.

quick.overview:
Bazedoxifene is a prescription SERM used for osteoporosis prevention and, with conjugated estrogens, for menopausal symptoms.
Published research concerns bone and menopause; no studies on appearance exist.
quick.mechanism: It binds estrogen receptors and acts like estrogen in bone while blocking estrogen in tissues such as the uterus, per preclinical work.
quick.risks: The combination product carries a boxed warning for endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia. Common effects include muscle spasms, nausea and diarrhea. It is prescription-only and contraindicated in pregnancy.

chain: Estrogen-like action in bone, blocking action in uterus and breast tissue
Preserved bone density in postmenopausal women
angle.text: Bazedoxifene is prescribed to keep bone strong after menopause and, with conjugated estrogens, to ease menopausal symptoms. In physique communities it is mentioned in the same breath as Nolvadex and Clomid as a newer member of the SERM family.
